story: Bharata was the son of Kaikeyi, who forced Rama's exile so that Bharata could be king. Bharata was horrified. He went to the forest to beg Rama to come back, and when Rama refused, he placed Rama's sandals on the throne and ruled for 14 years as Rama's servant.
belief: Bharata is remembered as the model of humility and selfless duty, proof that power can be refused. Bharat Milap, his reunion with Rama, is celebrated with great emotion in many places.
turns: He turned away from his own mother for what she had done. Some read his refusal to rule in his own right as too rigid, but most tellings praise it.
facts: He lived as an ascetic in Nandigram, outside Ayodhya, for all 14 years.
Rama's sandals on the throne are known as the paduka.
He vowed to give up his life if Rama was even one day late in returning.
lessons: Power you didn't earn isn't yours to take.
Hold a place faithfully until its rightful owner returns.
Love can mean refusing a gift.
more: The Bharat Milap at Nati Imli in Varanasi has celebrated his reunion with Rama for centuries.
Tradition links his son Taksha to the ancient city of Takshashila (Taxila).
